text: mirai package provides low-level future-like mechanism evaluating R expression separate R processes running local machine one remote machines. Centrally mirai highly-optimized queueing mechanism, used orchestrate communication main R process parallel workers. mirai cluster workers can configured communicate securely via well-established Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol. R (>= 4.4.0), can increase limit launch R, e.g. R --max-connections=200. title: Mirai-based cluster futures — mirai_cluster
text: access high-performance-compute (HPC) environment job scheduler, can use future.mirai mirai run parallel workers distributed computer cluster. set workers explained mirai::cluster_config(), work common job schedulers, e.g. Slurm, Sun/Son /Oracle/Univa/Altair Grid Engine (SGE), OpenLava, Load Sharing Facility (LSF), TORQUE/PBS. Note: compute clusters support running mirai workers way. mirai workers need establish TCP connection back machine launched workers, systems security policies disallowing connections established. often configured firewall can controlled admins. system rules, find mirai jobs launched running scheduler, wait forever mirai workers connect back, .e. mirai::info()[["connections"]] always zero example. Briefly, launch cluster mirai workers HPC cluster, need : configure mirai::cluster_config() job scheduler, use configuration launch workers using mirai::daemons(). first step specific job scheduler control things much memory worker gets, long may run, environment modules load, environment modules load, . second step regardless job scheduler. example run parallel mirai workers Slurm scheduler use futureverse.   SGE, can use following configuration:   Everything else . Comment: mirai::cluster_config() configures jobs run vanilla POSIX shells, .e. /bin/sh. might strict users. setup requires jobs run using Bash (/bin/sh), can tweak configuration config object manually ;
code: # Here we give each worker 200 MiB of RAM and a maximum of one hour # to run. Unless we specify '--cpus-per-task=N', each mirai worker # is allotted one CPU core, which prevents nested parallelization. # R is provided via environment module 'r' on this cluster. config <- mirai::cluster_config(command = "sbatch", options = "   #SBATCH --job-name=mirai   #SBATCH --time=01:00:00   #SBATCH --mem=200M   module load r ")  # ------------------------------------------------------------------- # Launch eight mirai workers, via equally many jobs, wait for all of # them to become available, and use them in futureverse # ------------------------------------------------------------------- workers <- 8 mirai::daemons(n = workers, url = mirai::host_url(), remote = config) while(mirai::info()[["connections"]] < workers) Sys.sleep(1.0) plan(future.mirai::mirai_cluster)  # Verify that futures are resolved on a compute node f <- future({   data.frame(     hostname = Sys.info()[["nodename"]],           os = Sys.info()[["sysname"]],        cores = unname(parallelly::availableCores()),      modules = Sys.getenv("LOADEDMODULES")   ) }) info <- value(f) print(info) #>   hostname    os cores  modules #> 1      n12 Linux     1  r/4.5.1  # Shut down parallel workers plan(sequential) mirai::daemons(0) config <- mirai::cluster_config(command = "qsub", options = "   #$ -N mirai   #$ -j y   #$ -cwd   #$ -l h_rt=01:00:00   #$ -l mem_free=200M   module load r ") config$command <- "/bin/bash" config$args <- sub("/bin/sh", config$command, config$args)

title: Version 0.10.0
text: Now ‘mirai’ futures can canceled using cancel(), also interrupts default, turn frees compute resources sooner. Map-reduce API future.apply, doFuture, furrr can take advantage canceling non-resolved futures whenever detect error one futures. Also, canceled futures can reset() thereafter relaunched, possibly another future backend. Now ‘mirai_multisession’ futures relay immediateCondition:s near real-time, e.g. progression conditions signals progressr package.
